name: MuJoCo
title: Try a different world.
intro: Take one moment in a robot's run and see two futures unfold together. Change the ground, gravity or a sideways shove, then scrub to the moment they part ways.
alt: A Unitree Go2 in the native MuJoCo viewer, comparing two futures with a shared timeline and body-height measurements.
scene: A real MuJoCo session: a 100 N sideways force for 0.15 seconds, with the same recorded controls in both worlds.
prompt: Load the Unitree Go2 and make it stand, then do three slow squats. Record the motion so I can open What if, change the surface friction and compare what happens from the same moment.

steps.title: Catch a moment
steps.text: Open What if, choose a body to follow and pin the current state.

steps.title: Change one thing
steps.text: Try Slippery ground or Lunar gravity, then Compare futures. Scrub both worlds together, or click Farthest apart to inspect the greatest sampled difference.

steps.title: Keep the experiment
steps.text: Save experiment preserves the model, its assets, the starting state, controls and measured frames. Measurements CSV keeps the numbers too.

keeps: A reproducible physics experiment and measurements CSV.
followup: Read my saved physics-experiment.json and reproduce it with the MuJoCo experiment tool. Explain when the robot first loses height, then help me change the controller and record another run.
note: Both futures use the same recorded controls. This compares open-loop physics; it does not rerun the Python controller.

name: Blender
title: Shape it until it feels right.
intro: Ask for the controls that matter to your design. Turn them yourself, watch Blender rebuild the geometry, and keep the directions you want to come back to.
alt: Shape Lab displaying a sculptural ribbon lamp with adjustable dimensions and a shelf of saved designs.
scene: A real Blender build of an authored ribbon lamp, with saved design variants.
prompt: Design a sculptural desk lamp from twisting ribbons. Give me Shape Lab controls for height, twist, ribbon count and finish, with sensible ranges. I want to explore the proportions myself and keep a few directions before the final render.

steps.title: Choose your controls
steps.text: Ask the agent for meaningful Shape Lab controls in the scene it builds. The starter mug already has a set to try.

steps.title: Find a direction
steps.text: Change the values and build a preview. Orbit the actual geometry, keep a named design and compare it with another.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.text: Download a kept design's project ZIP. Use values on next build carries your chosen values into the agent's next full export and render.

keeps: Source, chosen values, model, measurements and a standalone rebuild script.
followup: Use my chosen Shape Lab values for the next build. Refine the base and cable opening without losing these proportions, then export the model and render a turntable.
note: Each preview builds real Blender geometry. Build time depends on the scene; previews stay separate from the main export until the next full build.

name: Godogen
title: Try that moment again.
intro: Miss a jump, rewind and try another move. When something feels great or needs work, pin the exact moment so the agent can see what you mean.
alt: A playable game paused on its Rewind timeline with Try from here and Pin moment controls.
scene: A real playable browser game, including state restoration and saved playtest feedback.
prompt: Make a small rooftop delivery game with three jumps, a visible destination and forgiving controls. Make Rewind and Try from here work for the complete game state, so I can replay a difficult moment and leave useful playtest notes.

steps.title: Play a little
steps.text: Enter Play in a game with Rewind support. The viewer remembers the recent run while you play.

steps.title: Try another move
steps.text: Open Rewind and scrub back. Try from here resumes from that state; returning to the live moment restores the run you left.

steps.title: Pin what matters
steps.text: Pin moment with a Keep, Change or Explore note. Saved moments reopens that game version, screenshot and state after later edits.

keeps: A screenshot, complete game state, feedback and that version's compiled game.
followup: Read the saved playtest moments in out/playtests. Make the jump in my Change note easier to read, preserve the movement I marked Keep, then let me play the revised version.
note: Rewind needs snapshot support in the authored game. Saved moments preserve compiled output; editable source stays in the project, and external assets still need their original service.

name: Strudel
title: Perform the version you love.
intro: A track is an instrument you can play. Bring voices in and out, try a code change and mark the part you want to hear again. Keep the sound of that performance.
alt: Strudel's live voice lanes beside a recorded take with waveform, named moments and an audio-and-source download.
scene: A real performance of the original Lantern room track. The video includes the captured audio.
prompt: Write a warm 96 bpm evening groove with drums, a rounded bass, soft chords and a small bell melody. Use synths so it works offline, name the voices, and leave space for me to mute, solo and record a live take.

steps.title: Start the instrument
steps.text: Click Play, listen to the voices and choose Record take when you are ready.

steps.title: Perform it
steps.text: Mute or solo a voice, run a code change and mark a moment. Finish take opens the captured stereo audio with a seekable waveform.

steps.title: Keep the sound
steps.text: Name the performance and Keep take. Reopen it from Takes or download Audio + source to carry it away.

keeps: A stereo WAV, played code versions and a timed performance journal in a ZIP.
followup: Listen to the take I kept and read its journal in out/takes. Build the next arrangement around the quiet section I marked, using the source version that was playing there.
note: Takes capture up to two minutes of the instrument's output. The WAV preserves what you heard from it; external samples and custom imports are not bundled.

name: RDKit
title: See a molecule turn.
intro: Choose a flexible bond and move through its sampled shapes. Watch atoms approach one another, follow the calculated energy curve and keep a pose worth investigating.
alt: An authored molecule in 3D with a reference pose, native MMFF94 bond-energy curve and a selected rotation angle.
scene: A native RDKit bond scan on an authored molecule, shown with its starting conformer.
prompt: Build a 3D conformer of 2-phenylethanol with explicit hydrogens. I want to explore a flexible non-ring single bond in Bond scan, compare its shapes and understand where steric crowding raises the rigid MMFF94 energy.

steps.title: Pick a bond
steps.text: Open Bond scan and Use current conformer. Choose a four-atom chain, or measure a dihedral with T and four atom clicks.

steps.title: Explore its shapes
steps.text: Scan bond, then drag the energy curve, scrub the rotation or jump to the lowest sampled point. Compare against the starting pose.

steps.title: Keep a study
steps.text: Choose a pose, add a note and Keep study. Download the full scan and its Python reproducer, or reopen it from the saved library.

keeps: Input and sampled conformers, selected SDF, energy CSV and reproducible calculation source.
followup: Read the note and selected.sdf from my kept study in out/torsions. Reproduce its energy curve, explain the crowded poses and suggest another bond to explore.
note: This is a rigid MMFF94 scan, with the other internal coordinates fixed. It does not establish a relaxed barrier, equilibrium population or biological activity.

name: Typst
title: Point at what you mean.
intro: Hold a draft still while you read it. Quote a sentence, circle a detail or leave a page note, then compare the next draft without losing the one you reviewed.
alt: A native PDF draft held for review, with anchored Change, Keep and Question notes.
scene: A real Typst PDF rendered by pdf.js, with review notes carried into a later revision.
prompt: Make a two-page design brief for a small desk lamp: the idea, intended use, dimensions, materials and three open questions. Use Typst and give it a clear visual hierarchy. I want to review the PDF in the pane before we revise it.

steps.title: Hold this draft
steps.text: Open Review and Hold this draft. The exact PDF stays still while the agent continues working.

steps.title: Point and explain
steps.text: Select text and Note selected text, Pin an area or add a Page note. Mark it Change, Keep or Question and write what you mean.

steps.title: Carry it forward
steps.text: Keep review, then ask the agent to read its review.md. Compare latest deliberately; unique exact quotations can follow text to another page.

keeps: The reviewed PDF, anchored notes, readable feedback and a portable review ZIP.
followup: Read the kept review in .harness/doc-reviews, including review.md and reference.pdf. Revise the editable Typst source around my Change notes and preserve the details marked Keep.
note: Changed or repeated quotations need human inspection. Area and page notes stay with the reviewed PDF. The packet includes the PDF and feedback; editable source stays in the workspace.

name: Jev Sheets
title: Ask a better question.
intro: Before asking a whole spreadsheet, compare two versions of a question on frozen rows. Read the answers side by side and use your judgment to decide what the wording missed.
alt: Question Lab comparing two urgency questions on fictional support rows, prominently labeled offline practice.
scene: Offline practice with fictional rows. The demo shows the workflow, not Jev's live judgment quality.
prompt: Help me turn our support tickets into a sheet. Start with an urgency question, then suggest clearer wording to compare in Question Lab. I want to review a small sample and the unsure rows before asking the entire file.

steps.title: Freeze a sample
steps.text: Open Question Lab, choose an existing question and write a candidate. Preview 10, 20 or 40 rows and inspect the exact text and context.

steps.title: Compare the wording
steps.text: Compare asks both versions together. Inspect changed answers and full probabilities, then mark Original, New wording or Unsure and add your notes.

steps.title: Keep your reasoning
steps.text: Keep this trial saves the evidence. Try on whole sheet adds the candidate as a separate column; ask the agent to retain the chosen header in sheet.json.

keeps: Frozen rows, exact questions, answers, probabilities, provider details, your notes and CSV/ZIP exports.
followup: Read my kept trial in .harness/question-trials, including the rows and review.md. Help me choose clearer wording and retain that header in sheet.json before running the whole file.
note: Real answers send sampled rows to your connected Jev provider and require a key. Offline mode is practice only. Confidence and reviewer preferences are not measures of accuracy.

name: CircuitJS
title: See what changed in the signal.
intro: Capture a circuit, turn a component value and overlay the new trace. Place two cursors around the part that interests you and keep the observations with the circuit that produced them.
alt: Scope Lab comparing native RC filter traces at two resistance values with A and B measurement cursors.
scene: A native CircuitJS RC filter at two resistance values, captured by its real solver.
prompt: Build a 100 Hz RC low-pass filter with a 1 kΩ resistor and 1 µF capacitor. Label the input and output nodes. I want to capture both in Scope Lab, double the resistance and compare the amplitude and timing.

steps.title: Capture a window
steps.text: Open Scope Lab, choose named nodes or component voltage/current, select a duration and Capture circuit.

steps.title: Compare a change
steps.text: Change a component in the circuit and capture again. Choose the earlier take in Compare with; place A and B cursors and zoom between them.

steps.title: Keep both traces
steps.text: Name each take, record what you noticed and Keep capture. Your captures reopens saved traces; Download capture.zip carries the circuit and observations away.

keeps: Native circuit exports, timestamped measurements, an SVG plot, notes and a checksummed ZIP.
followup: Read both kept captures in .harness/circuit-captures. Compare their CSV measurements and my notes, explain what changing the resistance did, then help me choose the next circuit value to try.
note: Each capture starts a separate native simulation from the current circuit export. It uses a fresh time origin; initial transients can differ. Keep both captures to preserve a comparison.
